about: Cases where roc-font deliberately or knowingly differs from its recorded oracle result. scripts/conformance.py fails on any unlisted difference and on any listed case that now agrees; it never edits this file. Keep entries sorted by id; every entry needs a reason a reader can act on.

entries.reason: avar version 2 is out of scope for 0.1.0: roc-font drops the font's variation space (`Font.axes` is empty, so the driver answers `coords:`), where HarfBuzz applies avar2 and reports the normalised coordinates.

OTS rejects the font because it has no `OS/2` table: OTS requires `OS/2`, `name` and `post` to be present. roc-font rejects a broken `OS/2`, `name` or `post` as OTS does (architecture §4.4) but does not require them to be present, so callers can read metrics-only and synthetic fonts; accepting the font is a deliberate divergence.

The subset's glyf sets the reserved cubic flag bit (0x80) on a point; OTS 9.3.0 rejects the font ("Bad glyph flag") and roc-font follows OTS (architecture §4.4), while HarfBuzz reads it and reports coordinates.

HarfBuzz applies Apple-style `kern` tables (version 1.0, formats 0 and 2) and splits each value into an advance and an offset. OTS drops every `kern` table but version 0, so a browser never applies this one; roc-font drops it as OTS does (architecture §4.4, `corpus-fonts/jellee-kern-read` agrees), so the pairs are not kerned. Deliberate: browser parity over HarfBuzz parity for legacy tables.

OTS 9.3.0 rejects the font: its `GSUB` has a `DFLT` script without a default language system (ots/src/layout.cc lines 98-102), so a browser cannot draw it. roc-font refuses it as OTS does (architecture §4.4), where HarfBuzz shapes it anyway.

The font has a zero-length `glyf` table, for which OTS (and so every browser) rejects it; lenient reading accepts exactly what OTS accepts (architecture §4.4), so roc-font rejects the font where HarfBuzz shapes with it. Deliberate.

OTS 9.3.0 rejects the font: its only character map is a Macintosh (1, 0) format 0 subtable, and OTS refuses a font without a Unicode or Windows map it passes on (ots/src/cmap.cc lines 859-863), so a browser cannot draw it. roc-font refuses it as OTS does (architecture §4.4), where HarfBuzz decodes the Macintosh map.

TestKERNOne.otf is a CFF font with a `kern` table. OTS drops `kern` from fonts without `glyf` (its serializer: "this table is not for CFF fonts"), so browsers never kern it; roc-font drops it as OTS does (architecture §4.4) where HarfBuzz applies it. Deliberate.

OTS rejects the metrics-only subset because it has no `name` table: OTS requires `OS/2`, `name` and `post` to be present. roc-font rejects a broken `name` as OTS does (architecture §4.4) but does not require one, so accepting the font is a deliberate divergence.
